question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(-1,-2)$ to the point $B(3,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(-1+4t)\,i+(-2+6t)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=-i-2\,j$ and $b=3\,i+4\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(-i-2\,j)+t[(3\,i+4\,j)-(-i-2\,j)] \\  & =(-i-2\,j)+t(4\,i+6\,j) \\  & =(-1+4t)\,i+(-2+6t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=-1+4t,\,y=-2+6t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-1+4t+2-6t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(-1+4t-2+6t)\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(1-2t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(10t-3)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1+4t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2+6t)j \\  & =4\,i+6\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1-2t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(10t-3)\,j)\cdot (4\,i+6\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(1-2t)\cdot 4+\operatorname{sin}⁡(10t-3)\cdot 6 \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡(1-2t)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(10t-3).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4\operatorname{cos}⁡(1-2t)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(10t-3)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
